claim.quote: This measurement is the first one based on the direct detection of the photon pair and one of the most precise for positron energies below 1 GeV.

date.note: arXiv submission date (v1, 26 October 2022); the arXiv listing says the paper was submitted to Phys. Rev. D.

key_value_text.quote: The measurement agrees with the Next to Leading Order QED prediction within the overall 6% uncertainty.
key_value_text.value: e⁺e⁻ → γγ cross-section agrees with the next-to-leading-order QED prediction within an overall 6% uncertainty (430 MeV positrons)

name: Cross-section measurement of two-photon annihilation in-flight of positrons at sqrt(s)=20 MeV with the PADME detector
notes: The arXiv listing's comment says 'Submitted to PRD'; no journal reference was fetched.

summary.plain: PADME measured how often a positron and an electron annihilate into two photons in flight, at a collision energy of 20 MeV, by detecting both photons directly. The result agrees with QED calculations to within 6% and is a first step for dark-sector searches.
summary.technical: PADME (Run I/II data): inclusive e⁺e⁻ → γγ cross-section from 430 MeV positrons on a thin diamond target, √s about 20 MeV, using the BGO electromagnetic calorimeter; the first measurement based on direct detection of the photon pair; agrees with the NLO QED prediction within the overall 6% uncertainty.

title: Cross-section measurement of two-photon annihilation in-flight of positrons at sqrt(s)=20 MeV with the PADME detector
why_it_matters: The abstract calls it the first measurement based on direct detection of the photon pair and a necessary step for dark-sector searches with PADME.
